newsitem.title: USA: Darling pleads guilty to indictment count.
newsitem.headline: Darling pleads guilty to indictment count.

text.p: Darling International Inc. said Monday it has agreed to plead guilty to five counts of an indictment by a federal grand jury in Minnesota and pay $4 million in criminal, civil and administrative liabilities for waste water violations.
Darling is the nation's largest food waste recycler, turning restaurant grease and meat processing byproducts into chemicals and animal feed.
The agreement with the U.S. Attorney for the District of Minnesota resolves various waste water violations at its rendering plant in Blue Earth, Minn., between 1991 and 1993.
Darling said it has completed about $1.5 million worth of upgrades and improvements at the plant since 1992 to manage waste water better.
The Irving, Calif.-based company said it had also fired four employees, one of whom was involved in the indictment.
It said it has already recorded a loss provision of $6.1 million to cover the fines, penalties and other expenses it would incur as a result of the indictment.
Darling's stock rose $1.50 to $30.50 on Nasdaq.
